description.narrative: (Philippines): Fish Right supports the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) to apply ecosystem-based fisheries management (EBFM) in 48 LGUs across three marine key biodiversity areas. The partnership trains local governments on EBFM to help them set up management boards and science advisory councils, facilitate planning, and establish harvest control measures (HCMs) for ecologically important fish stocks. Building EBFM capacities in fisheries management areas (FMAs) will also increase local conservation actions. In the Calamianes Island Group (CIG), USAID will work with small-scale fishers, youth, women, and indigenous people to foster support for HCMs. As increased sea surface temperature and wave exposure due to changing climate has impacted coastal habitats, establishing marine protected area (MPA) networks and improving their management effectiveness will be supported to maximize habitat protection. Mangrove management and rehabilitation will also be supported to improve fish productivity and protect communities from extreme weather events. Fish Right will also address illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing through the nationwide roll out of a monitoring tool in more than 100 coastal cities in at least four FMAs. USAID will also work with universities to improve analytics on major illegal fishing hotspots. Satellite imagery will be used to analyze spatial distribution of marine resources in CIG and understand the ecological connection of marine systems of Palawan with the West Philippine Sea. Remote sensing data will help restore mangroves in women-managed areas and support women-led livelihoods. USAID will partner with the private sector to accelerate sustainable value chains' recovery from COVID-19, address post-harvest loss, and set up responsible seafood sourcing protocols.
